key_gap: AI found 3 of 5 planted flaws (bonus gaming, open-gated-survey selection bias, premature newsletter publication) and approved the plan with conditions — but missed the two fatal ones sitting in plain text: the security/privacy hole (ticket PII + password-reset tokens copied to pre-SOC2 staging with a public unauthenticated export endpoint, shared admin login, no SSO, no DPIA) and the unmodeled stakeholder (enterprise customers' 60–90-day vendor-risk review vs a 2-week go-live; legal/DPO absent). Its conditional approval therefore approved the breach and the timeline collision. The human red team found all five, ranked them by likelihood × impact, and blocked as written with six conditions.
learning_signal: Adversarial review earns its value in the non-obvious plane: incentive and metric flaws are pattern-recognizable (Goodhart, selection bias), but security/privacy and stakeholder-timeline flaws also sit in the plan's own text and are the fatal ones — 'fix the bonus and approve' while PII moves to an unauthenticated pre-SOC2 staging is approving a breach. Complete red teaming = attack every line item as hostile (data movement, auth model, publication, timeline vs external approval cycles), rank findings by likelihood × impact, and render a verdict where only a non-empty blocker list prevents conditional approval.
suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory adversarial-review checklist to the HOW stage for any plan/migration proposal: (1) incentives — what each actor gains by gaming each metric; (2) metrics — population vs gated sample, direction of bias, vanity inputs; (3) data movement — every copy/migration: what data (PII, secrets/tokens), where it lands (staging/prod, certification state), auth model, DPIA and legal sign-off; (4) stakeholders — who outside the plan must approve (customer procurement/security reviews with their cycle times, legal/DPO, frontline operators) and what their timelines are; (5) publication — what is claimed publicly and what data validity supports it. Packet must label every finding blocker-vs-non-blocker; conditional approval requires an empty blocker list. Verification must re-read the plan text line by line, not just re-derive already-drawn conclusions.

key_gap: The human red team blocked a sound, reversible, urgent MFA rollout (EHR access with 41 shared passwords, 3 leaked credentials, and an active brute-force attempt last month) on unranked hypotheticals — key loss, auth-server outage, vendor firmware, missing SOC 2 addendum — treating every objection at full severity and password-only login as risk-free. The AI found the same objections but likelihood-ranked them (rejecting 4 of 5 as low-likelihood or already-mitigated), costed the status quo as the realized risk, and approved a staged rollout with rollback runbook and monitoring.
learning_signal: Red teaming without calibration is hazard theater: 'nothing is 100% secure' is true and irrelevant — the decision compares baseline risk (password-only with shared/leaked credentials, actively attacked) against mitigation risk (MFA with 99.99% SLA, <15-min lockout recovery, tested one-flag rollback). Inaction is a decision with its own risk; every objection needs likelihood × impact, and 'could happen' is not a blocker where the baseline is already failing. The high-value move is the inaction-cost line, which the uncalibrated style never writes.
suggested_improvement: Add a status-quo-costing gate to every go/no-go review path in the agent: before any objection may block, the packet must contain (1) an explicit baseline-risk line — what the current state costs, evidenced (audit findings, observed attacks), not asserted; (2) a likelihood × impact rank per objection; (3) a reject-objection log — each false alarm dismissed with its rejecting evidence (SLA, pilot data, rollback test, artifact-vs-functional distinction); (4) an inaction-cost sentence ('delay keeps exposure X active'). Blocking is permitted only when the blocker list survives this gate; otherwise the verdict must be a reversible, time-boxed approval with monitoring.

key_gap: Human caught all 4 planted flaws incl. code enumeration with quantified farm economics; AI never analyzed the enumeration vector.
learning_signal: Adversary-modeling must include exploit-vector analysis (guessable formats, identity gates) with quantified exposure, not deferral.
suggested_improvement: Add an adversary-modeling sub-step for money/fraud-adjacent gates: enumerated inputs, quantified exposure.

key_gap: Human blocked a sound go-live on unranked HIGHs; AI falsified inaction-is-risk-free and approved a staged canary.
learning_signal: Adversarial attack must be calibrated against baseline risk: state do-nothing expected loss before alternatives.
suggested_improvement: Add a baseline-risk gate: do-nothing loss, objections ranked by LxI, time-boxed decision bar with abort criteria.
